definitions.explanation: To agree to take or allow something.

definitions.gloss: to accept, to come to terms with
definitions.explanation: To acknowledge and accept a situation or reality.

examples.japanese: {提案|ていあん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れた。
{難民|なんみん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる。
{条件|じょうけん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れることにした。
examples.english: I decided to accept the conditions.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{留学生|りゅうがくせい}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる{準備|じゅんび}をしている。
examples.english: We are preparing to accept new exchange students.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{彼|かれ}の{要求|ようきゅう}をすべて{受|う}け{入|い}れて、{新|あたら}しい{契約|けいやく}を{結|むす}んだ。
examples.english: The company accepted all his demands and signed a new contract.

examples.japanese: {現実|げんじつ}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる。
{結果|けっか}を{受|う}け{入|い}れなければならない。
{自分|じぶん}の{失敗|しっぱい}を{受|う}け{入|い}れるのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's hard to accept one's own failures.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{時間|じかん}をかけて{別|わか}れを{受|う}け{入|い}れた。
examples.english: She took time to come to terms with the breakup.

examples.japanese: {変|か}えられないことは{受|う}け{入|い}れて、{変|か}えられることに{力|ちから}を{注|そそ}いだほうがいい。
examples.english: It's better to accept what you can't change and focus your energy on what you can.

notes:
{受|う}け{入|い}れる means to accept, receive, or come to terms with something.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}). Compound of {受|う}ける + {入|い}れる.

TWO MAIN USAGES:
1. To accept/receive (proposals, people): {提案|ていあん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる
2. To accept/come to terms with: {現実|げんじつ}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {受|う}け{入|い}れ: acceptance (noun form)
- {受|う}け{入|い}れ{態勢|たいせい}: reception preparation
- {難民|なんみん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる: to accept refugees
- {条件|じょうけん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる: to accept conditions
- {批判|ひはん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる: to accept criticism

CONTRAST:
- {受|う}け{入|い}れる: to accept (actively agree to)
- {受|う}ける: to receive (more passive)
